target_audience: High school students and undergraduate STEM enthusiasts

sections.title: The Concept of Dimensionality
lecture_lines: Dimensions are directions of movement in space.
A line is 1D, allowing movement back and forth.
Linus the line-worm only sees points in 1D.
To see length, he needs a second dimension.
Shifting to 2D reveals his world from sideways.
animations: Create a single white point (#FFFFFF) at the origin.
Transform the point into a thin green horizontal line segment (#00FF00) of length 4.
Add a small red circle (#FF0000) representing 'Linus' onto the line segment.
Scale and shift the perspective to show the line segment as part of a 2D plane.
Draw a blue arrow (#0000FF) perpendicular to the line to indicate the second dimension.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Projections and Cross-Sections
lecture_lines: Projections are shadows of higher-dimensional objects.
A cross-section is a slice of a 3D shape.
A sphere passing through 2D looks like a circle.
animations: Create a yellow 3D sphere (#FFFF00) and a semi-transparent gray horizontal plane (#888888) below it.
Move the sphere vertically downwards through the plane.
Show a cyan circle (#00FFFF) on the plane that starts as a point, grows to the sphere's radius, and then shrinks back to a point.

sections.title: The 2D-to-3D Shift: The Net Folding Puzzle
lecture_lines: Unfold 3D into 2D nets.
Nets show faces flat.
Shortest paths use lines.
animations: Create a white 3D cube wireframe (#FFFFFF).
Unfold the cube faces onto the XY plane to form a T-shape net in green (#00FF00).
Place two bright red dots (#FF0000) on the net at positions corresponding to opposite vertices of the cube.
Draw a thick blue straight line segment (#0000FF) connecting these two red dots on the flat net.
Animate the net folding back into the cube, showing the blue line segment becoming a path across multiple faces.

sections.title: The 3D-to-4D Shift: Visualizing the Tesseract
lecture_lines: The fourth dimension adds Ana and Kata directions.
A tesseract is the 4D version of a cube.
Its shadow appears as a cube within a cube.
4D rotation makes the cubes swap and distort.
This projection helps us visualize the fourth dimension.
animations: Draw a white square (#FFFFFF) on the screen.
Draw a smaller gray square (#888888) inside it and connect the corresponding vertices with gray lines.
Draw a white cube wireframe (#FFFFFF).
Draw a smaller gray cube wireframe (#888888) inside it and connect the corresponding vertices with gray lines.
Animate the vertices of the Tesseract projection shifting such that the inner cube expands and becomes the outer cube.

sections.title: Solving the 'Impossible' Geometry Puzzle
lecture_lines: Some puzzles are impossible in only three dimensions.
Interlocking rings cannot be unlinked in 3D space.
In 4D, they slide apart easily without breaking.
animations: Draw two interlocking circles, one magenta (#FF00FF) and one cyan (#00FFFF), in a 3D-like orientation.
Animate the circles moving toward each other and stopping as they 'collide' in 3D space.
Fade the magenta circle to 50% opacity and move it 'past' the cyan circle to show them separating.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Dimensional shifts simplify complex geometric problems.
These concepts help scientists map protein folding.
Mastering dimensions reveals hidden structures of our universe.
animations: Display the text 'N+1: Solve Obstacles' in green (#00FF00) and 'N-1: Gain Perspective' in blue (#0000FF).
Show a 1D chain of colored beads morphing into a complex 3D folded structure.
Fade everything out and show the final text 'Master the Dimensions' in white (#FFFFFF).
